text.p: These are the main stories in Latvian newspapers on Monday. Prepared for Reuters by the Co-operation Fund. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy:
- The Latvias Way conference decided that a Riga city council co-operation agreement has to be signed by four political forces representing the government forming parties.
- Latvia and Russia have agreed on the land border delimitation line and its final description. Another round of talks is due on April 26 in Moscow.
- Russian President Boris Yeltsin announced in Helsinki that Russia wants to guarantee the security of the Baltic states.
- Ligatne paper mill, in central Latvia, has been auctioned off for 454,000 lats. The starting price was 28,000 lats.
- State budget revenues exceeded expenditure by 2.47 million lats so far this year but the social insurance budget was 5.89 million lats short.
- The newspaper publishes an article arguing that the Latvian security police are hindering the registration of foreign companies in Latvia.
- Neste signed an oil terminal building contract with the port of Riga.
- Prime Minister Andris Shkele met with Israeli Ambassador Oded ben Hur. They discussed the possibility of opening a memorial centre to Holocaust victims in Riga.

- Mayor of Daugavpils, the second biggest city in Latvia, Aleksey Vidavskii, has gone on trial for violating the election law, which bars members of the Communist party after January 13, 1991 of taking public posts.
- Rietumu bank has opened its first branch office in Daugavpils.

- The Latvian Chamber of Commerce and Industry signed a co-operation agreement with its South Westphalia counterpart in Hagen, Germany. The agreement aims at improving business training programs in Latvia.
- Aldaris, the largest brewery in Latvia, registerd sales of about 39.2 million litres of beer in 1996. The company's market share in Latvia reached 57 percent.
